Risk: Security responsibilities are unclear or unowned, so controls lapse without anyone noticing.
Typical causes: No named owner; security left to whoever has time; leadership not reviewing the program.
Brain fields to draw on: Team Details, Governance, Operating Cadence, Company Stage
Ask the client: Who owns security day to day? If something slipped, who would notice?

Risk: Someone commits fraud or overrides controls for personal gain, such as diverting payments or misusing access.
Typical causes: One person can set up and pay a vendor; admin access without oversight; pressure to hit targets.
Brain fields to draw on: Headcount, Company Stage, Access ownership, Governance
Ask the client: Who can approve payments or change bank details? Can one person both add a supplier and pay them?

Risk: A staff member mishandles data or falls for a scam through carelessness or lack of awareness.
Typical causes: No training; unclear rules on data and AI use; policies not acknowledged.
Brain fields to draw on: Headcount, Workforce model, Data Handled
Ask the client: How do people learn the security basics when they join? When did the team last have training?

Risk: Someone unsuitable is hired into a position of trust.
Typical causes: No reference or background checks; contractors skip hiring checks.
Brain fields to draw on: Country/Region(s), Workforce model, Headcount
Ask the client: Do you check references or run background checks? Is it different for contractors?

Risk: People who leave or change role keep access they no longer need.
Typical causes: No offboarding checklist; HR and IT not linked; accounts spread across many tools.
Brain fields to draw on: HR System, Identity and Authentication, Access ownership, Headcount
Ask the client: When someone leaves, who tells IT, and how long before their accounts are turned off?

Risk: Critical knowledge or admin access sits with one or two people, so the service stalls if they're unavailable.
Typical causes: Founder-held admin rights; undocumented runbooks; no backup for key roles.
Brain fields to draw on: Team Details, Headcount, Company Stage
Ask the client: If your lead engineer was unreachable for two weeks, could someone else deploy or restore?

Risk: Staff accounts are taken over through phishing, password reuse or stolen credentials.
Typical causes: MFA not enforced everywhere; shared or weak passwords; no single sign-on.
Brain fields to draw on: Identity and Authentication, Password Manager, Workspace
Ask the client: Is MFA switched on for everyone, everywhere? Do people use a password manager?

Risk: Excessive or privileged access is misused, deliberately or by mistake.
Typical causes: Standing admin rights; access never reviewed; shared admin accounts; long-lived keys.
Treating controls: AC-03A, AC-03B, AC-04, AC-05A, AC-05B, AC-05C, AC-06, AC-15
Brain fields to draw on: Privileged & production access, Access ownership, Privileged Access Management
Ask the client: Who has admin access to production today? Would that list surprise anyone?

Risk: Staff view or change customer data without a valid reason.
Typical causes: Broad support access; no approval or logging of data access.
Treating controls: AC-13A, AC-13B, AC-13C, AC-14, LM-01A, LM-01B
Brain fields to draw on: Provider access to customer data, Customer administration
Ask the client: When would anyone on your team look at a customer's data? Who allows it, and is it logged?

Risk: One customer's data is exposed to another customer.
Typical causes: Shared databases without tenant checks; bugs in access logic; missing tests.
Brain fields to draw on: Tenancy & isolation, Databases
Ask the client: How is each customer's data kept separate? Is that tested?

Risk: Customer data is exposed through misconfigured storage, databases or public endpoints.
Typical causes: Public buckets; open database ports; settings drift with no checks.
Brain fields to draw on: Databases, Infrastructure, Cloud Configuration Monitoring
Ask the client: How would you know if a database or bucket became public?

Risk: Data is intercepted in transit or read from storage because encryption is missing or weak.
Typical causes: Old TLS; unencrypted backups or disks; keys managed by hand.
Brain fields to draw on: Databases, Application Secrets and Encryption, Edge and Web Protection
Ask the client: Is customer data encrypted everywhere it's stored, including backups?

Risk: Secrets, keys or tokens leak, for example through code or chat, and are used to get in.
Typical causes: Secrets committed to repositories; keys shared in messages; no rotation.
Brain fields to draw on: Application Secrets and Encryption, Code Repository, Software Vulnerability Scanning
Ask the client: Where do your API keys and secrets live? What happens if one leaks?

Risk: Data is kept longer than needed, or not deleted when promised to customers.
Typical causes: No retention schedule; deletion done by hand; backups kept indefinitely.
Brain fields to draw on: Data Handled, Service Commitments, Data minimisation
Ask the client: What happens to a customer's data when they leave? How long do you keep it?

Risk: Sensitive data leaves through email, sharing links, personal accounts or unapproved apps.
Typical causes: Open sharing settings; no data rules; personal devices and accounts used for work.
Brain fields to draw on: Workspace, Data Loss Prevention, Endpoint model
Ask the client: Can files be shared publicly or outside the company? Do people use personal accounts for work?

Risk: A lost or stolen laptop exposes company or customer data.
Typical causes: Unencrypted disks; no device inventory; no remote wipe.
Brain fields to draw on: Device Management, Endpoint model, Workforce model
Ask the client: Are all laptops encrypted? Could you wipe one remotely?

Risk: Malware or ransomware infects staff devices or servers.
Typical causes: No endpoint protection; delayed updates; unrestricted software installs.
Brain fields to draw on: Endpoint Protection, Device Management, Backups and Recovery
Ask the client: What protects laptops from malware? Who sees the alerts?

Risk: An unauthorised or untested change breaks production or introduces a vulnerability.
Typical causes: Direct pushes to production; no peer review; manual deployments; untracked infrastructure changes.
Treating controls: CM-01, CM-02A, CM-02B, CM-03A, CM-03B, CM-04A, CM-04B, CM-06A, CM-06B, CM-06C, CM-08A, CM-08B
Brain fields to draw on: Change management, Release Frequency, Code Repository, Build and Deployment / CI/CD, Infrastructure Configuration
Ask the client: Can anyone get code into production without a second person looking at it?

Risk: Vulnerable code or third-party libraries are exploited.
Typical causes: No dependency scanning; no secure coding practice; findings not fixed.
Brain fields to draw on: Software Vulnerability Scanning, Code Repository, Penetration Test Status
Ask the client: How do you find out about vulnerable libraries? How fast are they fixed?

Risk: An unpatched infrastructure vulnerability is exploited.
Typical causes: Self-managed servers; no scanning; patching left to chance.
Brain fields to draw on: Infrastructure, Infrastructure operations, Infrastructure Vulnerability Scanning
Ask the client: Who patches servers and base images, and how often?

Risk: An attack or misuse goes unnoticed because activity isn't logged or alerted on.
Typical causes: Logs not collected or kept; alerts go nowhere; no one on call.
Brain fields to draw on: Audit Logging, Security Threat Detection, Incident response
Ask the client: If someone logged into production at 3am, would anyone know?

Risk: An incident is handled badly, or customers and regulators aren't told in time.
Typical causes: No plan or roles; plan never tested; notification deadlines unknown.
Brain fields to draw on: Incident response, Service Commitments, Regulatory Drivers, Country/Region(s)
Ask the client: Who would lead if you had a breach tonight? Who decides what customers are told?

Risk: Data is lost or the service is down for a long time because recovery doesn't work.
Typical causes: Backups untested; no recovery plan; single region; recovery steps known by one person.
Treating controls: BC-01A, BC-01B, BC-02, AV-01A, AV-01B, AV-02
Brain fields to draw on: Backups and Recovery, Availability responsibility, Hosting Platform
Ask the client: Have you ever restored from a backup? How long did it take?

Risk: The service can't meet its availability commitments.
Typical causes: No capacity planning; single points of failure; uptime not measured.
Treating controls: AV-03, AV-04A, AV-04B, AV-05A, AV-05B, AV-06, AV-07A, AV-07B
Brain fields to draw on: Availability responsibility, Auto-scaling, Availability Monitoring, Service Commitments
Ask the client: What uptime have you promised customers? How do you measure it?

Risk: A critical vendor or subservice provider fails, is breached or changes its terms.
Typical causes: No vendor review; no assurance reports; heavy reliance on one provider.
Treating controls: VM-01A, VM-01B, VM-02, VM-03, VM-05A, VM-05B
Brain fields to draw on: Subservice Providers, Infrastructure, Hosting Platform, Vendor management
Ask the client: Which vendors would stop your service if they went down or were breached?

Risk: Staff adopt tools without review, sharing company or customer data with unvetted vendors.
Typical causes: Free trials and personal sign-ups; no approval step; OAuth apps connected freely.
Brain fields to draw on: Vendor management, Workspace, AI Models and Platforms
Ask the client: Can anyone connect a new app to your workspace or sign up for a tool with a work email?

Risk: The company fails to meet what it has promised customers in contracts, terms or questionnaires.
Typical causes: Commitments not tracked; sales promises outrun controls; controls not mapped to commitments.
Brain fields to draw on: Service Commitments, Terms of Service, Customer Types
Ask the client: What have you promised customers about security, uptime or data? Who keeps track of it?

Risk: The company breaches privacy or data protection law.
Typical causes: Unclear legal obligations; overseas data transfers; requests from individuals not handled.
Brain fields to draw on: Regulatory Drivers, Customer Geography, Country/Region(s), Data Handled
Ask the client: Which privacy laws apply to you and your customers? Who handles privacy requests?

Risk: Confidential or customer data is entered into AI tools, or used to train third-party models.
Typical causes: No approved AI tool list; consumer AI accounts; provider terms not checked.
Brain fields to draw on: AI Models and Platforms, Data Handled
Ask the client: Which AI tools does the team use? Have you checked whether they train on your data?

Risk: An AI feature produces inaccurate, harmful or biased output that customers rely on.
Typical causes: No evaluation before release; no monitoring; customers treat output as final.
Brain fields to draw on: AI reliance, Responsibility for outcomes
Ask the client: Who checks AI output before customers see it? How would you know it was getting worse?

Risk: An AI agent takes unintended actions, or is manipulated through prompt injection.
Typical causes: Agents with broad permissions; no approval for high-impact actions; actions not logged.
Brain fields to draw on: AI reliance, Control execution, AI Models and Platforms
Ask the client: What can your agents do without a person approving it? Can you see what they did?

Risk: Automated or agent-run controls stop working and nobody notices.
Typical causes: No owner for automations; failed jobs not alerted; reliance on dashboards nobody checks.
Brain fields to draw on: Control execution, Compliance Automation
Ask the client: Which controls run automatically? Who would notice if one stopped?

Risk: Someone gains physical access to offices, equipment or devices at customer sites.
Typical causes: Unrestricted office entry; visitors not logged; equipment not tracked.
Brain fields to draw on: Facilities, Workforce model
Ask the client: Is there anywhere physical that holds sensitive equipment or paperwork?

Risk: Customers misconfigure their own security settings or integrations, leading to a breach that reflects on the service.
Typical causes: Weak defaults; unclear customer responsibilities; API keys poorly managed by customers.
Brain fields to draw on: Customer administration, Integration surface, System Description: CUECs
Ask the client: Which security settings do customers control themselves? Do you tell them what they're responsible for?

Risk: Planned changes such as new products, regions, AI features or acquisitions outpace security and compliance.
Typical causes: Changes planned without a security view; scope not updated; new tools added quickly.
Brain fields to draw on: Planned Changes, Target Compliance, Company Stage
Ask the client: What big changes are coming in the next 12 months?
